summary.text:
The 2025/26 Statement of Accounts went to Audit, Risk and Governance on 27 July 2026 as a covering report only. Appendix A carries the accounts themselves and is not held on disk, so there is no CFR, no external borrowing figure, no maturity profile, no prudential indicators and no MRP policy in what we've read. No reconciliation is possible from this paper.

What the covering report does surface is the DSG position: an in-year overspend of £79.2m against a £1,117.2m Dedicated Schools Grant on £1,196.4m of expenditure, £22.4m brought forward, leaving a £101.6m cumulative negative DSG reserve at 31 March 2026 under the statutory override. The February 2026 Local Government Finance Settlement provides a grant covering 90% of the High Needs-related portion, conditional on a SEND reform plan submitted by 19 June 2026 — the fraction of Lancashire's deficit that is High Needs-related is not printed in the covering report, so the residual exposure is not derivable from what we hold.

The other substantive item is the waste recycling facilities revaluation on the three-yearly cycle: Lancashire's 87.5% share moves from £51.82m (March 2023) to £200.03m (March 2026), a £148.21m uplift, valued by a new firm (Newmark Gerald Eve LLP) on the RICS Depreciated Replacement Cost basis. That will flow through PPE and depreciation — and via depreciation, the MRP profile going forward. The Code change on PPE revaluation, moving to a five-yearly cycle with BCIS-driven annual indexation, is also flagged.

From our own PWLB file, at 31 March 2026 Lancashire held 15 loans totalling £494.6m at a weighted 4.51%, all MATURITY. £185m sits within twelve months of year-end, of which £100m is in two £50m loans at 4.37% and 4.38% maturing 7 January 2027. Offered as a cross-check against Appendix A rather than as a claim.

Contact is Khadija Saeed, Head of Corporate Finance, with a published email on the paper. She is the named contact for this report, not the S151 (that is the Corporate Director of Finance, not named). Sending to her is appropriate. The specific committee meeting has passed; the next natural touchpoint is the approval-after-audit meeting, date not printed in this paper.

officer.body:
Hi Khadija,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. Normally that means we write with something specific about a council's own numbers. This one is a little shorter and more honest than most, because what we hold of your 2025/26 accounts is the covering report that went to Audit, Risk and Governance on 27 July — Appendix A, where every treasury figure lives, isn't in what we have. So nothing below is a comment on your position and we haven't guessed at one. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these.

The one place we can bring something to Appendix A runs the other way, from our data to you. Our PWLB file for Lancashire at 31 March 2026 shows 15 loans, £494.6m outstanding at a weighted 4.51%, all maturity profile. Since year-end £150m of that has already matured — two loans redeemed in the ordinary course — and a further £100m sits in two £50m loans at 4.37% and 4.38% falling due together on 7 January 2027. So half the year-end book was either off by August or reaches maturity within nine months of it, which is the sort of concentration a member might reasonably ask about at the approval meeting. We hold PWLB only — LOBOs, market debt and inter-authority borrowing sit outside our file — so Appendix A is the authoritative version and this is offered as a cross-check rather than a claim. What we hold for you is visible at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis.

The one substantive item the covering report does surface is the DSG position: a £79.2m in-year overspend against a £1,117.2m grant, £22.4m brought forward, £101.6m held against the statutory override at year end. Across the councils we've read, that shape is showing up more and more, and the piece audit committees are asking about is what happens after the February 2026 Settlement grant lands — 90% is on the High Needs-related deficit, conditional on the SEND reform plan submitted in June, and the balance sits above that. Where the deficit has drawn on cash rather than reserves it tends to surface in the liability benchmark, which is one of the two indicators the CIPFA Prudential and Treasury Code updates are pushing to the front of everyone's committee papers.

For context on the market Appendix A will describe: Bank Rate is 3.75%, one-year PWLB certainty closed at 4.95% on notice 314/26 and the twenty-five year at 6.46%, and July's sector borrowing was £368m across 33 loans from just 19 borrowers at an average 5.02% — a thin market, informative if any of that January 2027 £100m is refinanced at maturity rather than repaid. That monthly breakdown is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity.

On training, three would fit the papers going with an accounts approval. Liability Benchmark: the essentials, which is where any DSG-driven displacement will show up. MRP — policy options and revenue impact, because the waste recycling revaluation you describe in paragraphs 6 to 9 (£51.82m to £200.03m on your 87.5% share) will move the depreciation and MRP profile going forward. And Audit committee scrutiny for members, given this paper goes through Audit, Risk and Governance. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/
